clue.text: About a pound is reasonable for such a faculty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for reasonable is wrapped around the pound sign

parts.note: a reasonable price is a fair one
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a pound is a fair price for a mental gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A flair is a natural talent or aptitude, a gift for something.

clue.text: Up-to date Senior Service style

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
the Senior Service is the Royal Navy, abbreviated RN

explanation.surface: The Royal Navy shows off a fashionable new look.
explanation.walkthrough: The Senior Service is the British nickname for the Royal Navy, the oldest of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something current and fashionable is contemporary, of the present day.

clue.text: Pacifies with sausages and mash

indicators.note: to mash is to crush and mix up, so the letters of the word for bangers are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook calms people down with sausages and mashed potato, the classic British banger-and-mash dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Mash is mashed potato, served with sausages as bangers and mash, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or calm, so assuaging pacifies.

clue.text: Even chances in caber-throwing contests

definitions.meaning: a fifty-fifty outcome, as when a coin is flipped
Highland games events where a heavy pole is tossed upwards

explanation.surface: Who wins the Highland caber events is anyone's guess.
explanation.walkthrough: Caber-tossing is a Scottish Highland games event in which a long wooden pole is thrown end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip gives equal odds, and a caber contest is literally a series of throws upward.

clue.text: Get into difficulties with the fish

explanation.surface: Someone struggles while trying to deal with the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle clumsily is one meaning of the verb; a flatfish of the same name is the noun.

clue.text: Starts with stop, turns colour and it's over

parts.note: to stop somewhere is to stay or remain

indicators.note: turns tells us the colour word is flipped round end to end

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A traffic signal that starts at stop and changes colour signals the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts with' only says the answer opens with the word for stop; 'turns' flips RED to give DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A remainder is what is left over after the rest is gone.

clue.text: Red-eyed-due to passion?

parts.note: eyes reddened, read playfully as if a burst of hot blood had been fired into them

explanation.surface: Someone's eyes are red, perhaps from strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that are red and inflamed have tiny blood vessels showing.

clue.text: Passage for friend touring the Orient

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for friend surrounds the letter for the East

parts.note: an ally is a friend
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A traveller buys a ticket for a companion's trip around the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow lane or passageway between buildings.

clue.text: A sore point now and in past years

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something has been a sore point now and for years past.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore spot.

clue.text: Effigies with a knowing look?

parts.note: Bonfire Night dummies of Guy Fawkes, imagined as having a shrewd expression

explanation.surface: Bonfire dummies seem to wear a knowing look.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy is the straw effigy of Guy Fawkes burnt on Bonfire Night, 5 November, in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart alecks or know-alls are called by this American slang term, also used of mobsters.

clue.text: Really good guy, we hear, as president

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is matched by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a true man is a really good, honest fellow

explanation.surface: Voters judge a candidate a decent fellow, fit to be president.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S. Truman was the 33rd US president.

clue.text: Poles with a lot of dollars, but there's a drawback

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
G is a grand, a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Polish emigrants arrive with plenty of money, but there is a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden problem or obstacle.

clue.text: Entreaty notable soft in the first place

indicators.note: in the first place puts the letter for soft at the very front

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
a leading figure is a notable one

explanation.surface: A request from a prominent man softly spoken at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleading is an earnest appeal or plea.

clue.text: We're helped in marked surroundings

indicators.note: in places the pronoun within the word for marked
surroundings means the word for marked forms the wall around the pronoun

parts.note: stained means marked or soiled
we are, in the object form us

explanation.surface: We get support while in grubby, marked surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We're' supplies US, the object form of we, set inside STAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain someone is to support or keep them going.

clue.text: Set up in the most feeble way

indicators.note: way signals a manner of arranging, so the three words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is built in the weakest manner possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny means weak and small, so the superlative is the weakest.

clue.text: Acute as sin and vice I find

indicators.note: find suggests discovering a new arrangement, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone sharply observes that sin and vice are much alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisive mind is sharp and penetrating, keen-witted.

clue.text: It's quite common to leave without notice

definitions.text: It's quite common to leave without notice

parts.words: It's quite common to leave without notice
parts.note: a slangy, rather vulgar word for running off suddenly, common meaning low-register

explanation.surface: People often walk out without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Common here means coarse or slangy, not frequent; the answer is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for to run off or bolt.

clue.text: Shut up with Mr. Heath?

parts.note: read as a verb for shutting followed by the nickname of Edward Heath, or as being kept in private

explanation.surface: Someone is locked away with a former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath, British prime minister 1970-74, was known as Ted; CLOSE plus TED gives the word for shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shut away in private, as in a small room, is to be closeted.

clue.text: Express sympathy for the cabinet

definitions.meaning: a cabinet housing a radio, television or organ controls

explanation.surface: Someone comforts the government ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is the verb sense; a housing for a radio or the keyboard unit of an organ is the noun sense.

clue.text: Sounds abrupt in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: Sounds abrupt in a manner of speaking

parts.words: Sounds abrupt in a manner of speaking
parts.note: a style of delivery, musical or vocal, with each note clipped short and detached

explanation.surface: A person's talk comes across as curt.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato describes notes played short and separated, so speech in that style is clipped and jerky.

clue.text: A fish jelly? You can say that again

parts.note: the gar or garfish is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fishy jelly exists, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can say that again' hints at the doubled name agar-agar, by which the jelly is also known.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods and grow cultures.

clue.text: Honour given to an Arabian sultanate

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An honour is conferred on someone from a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: The country on the south-east of the Arabian peninsula is ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: A very quiet Scot way out from Rome

parts.note: pp is pianissimo, very quiet in music
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A taciturn Scotsman is on his way out of the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Appian Way was the great Roman road leading out of the city to the south-east.

clue.text: One bent on the staff

definitions.meaning: a dishonest person, bent being slang for corrupt

explanation.surface: A determined person sets their mind on the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: Bent is British slang for dishonest; 'on' is a link word, though it reads as 'bent on' meaning determined.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal is a swindler, and the hooked staff of a shepherd or bishop has the same name.

clue.text: Pollution on the motorway as Mother discovered

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A mother finds smog on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; its digit is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious, polluted vapour or atmosphere.

clue.text: See 27
Even trains running overhead don't disturb them

definitions.text: Even trains running overhead don't disturb them

parts.words: Even trains running overhead don't disturb them
parts.note: people who sleep soundly, with a pun on the wooden beams under railway lines that trains run over

explanation.surface: Some people sleep through anything, even trains rumbling above.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleepers are also the timber beams that railway lines rest on; trains do run over them, and they are not disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep slumberers are hard to wake, and railway ties bear heavy trains.

clue.text: A relation who could divide the family

definitions.text: A relation who could divide the family

indicators.note: dividing splits things up, so the letters of the opening two words are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative stirs up a family feud.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who estranges others turns them against each other, causing a rift.
